items.title: Origin Energy confirms customer data breached in hack
items.description: Energy company Origin confirms there has been unauthorised access to and disclosure of some customers' data, a day after it announced it was investigating a "potential" breach.

items.title: Oil prices jump back over $US100 a barrel as Middle East conflict widens
items.description: The entry of the Houthi rebels into the war between the US and Iran threatens another vital shipping route through the region, as the entire region remains on high alert.

items.title: Billions in new funding for AUKUS shipyards in Adelaide
items.description: The billions of dollars in additional funding is another step towards making Australia's nuclear submarine program "a reality".

items.title: Saudi Arabia must recognise Israel for nuclear deal, says Trump
items.description: Donald Trump is insisting the US deal allowing Saudi Arabia to develop a nuclear energy industry has one major condition — the Arab kingdom must formally recognise the State of Israel.

items.title: Labor debates future, Liberals hold up pamphlet
items.description: Australia's two major parties are deliberating their futures this week with Labor's national conference and the Liberal Party's glossy new pamphlet.

items.title: Chinese diplomats leave ALP conference after bid to eject Taiwan officials
items.description: The incident could stir fresh tensions between China and Australia in the wake of several recent high-profile disputes.

items.title: The former cocaine-dealing Sydney socialite linked to a far-right news site
items.description: A "right of centre" website claiming to be news, with more than 42,000 Facebook followers, may not be as independent as it says. An ABC NEWS Verify investigation has found the site uses AI and a fake news editor.

items.title: Bystanders praised for courage to stop attempted murder of woman
items.description: A man who "doggedly" tried to kill a woman in a prolonged attack in suburban Perth caught on CCTV has is been jailed for 16 years.

items.title: Researcher shocked as orca blows up a sunfish in front of her
items.description: Underwater video captures the moment killer whales in the Gulf of California slam into a sunfish, causing it to explode. Researchers say the orcas may use the technique to make it easier for juvenile killer whales to feed or they do it as a fun group bonding exercise.

items.title: Penrith flyer breaks record in comeback Panthers win
items.description: Thomas Jenkins has claimed a slice of history in Penrith's unconvincing win over Parramatta in the western Sydney derby.

items.title: Pies make statement with impressive win over listless Crows
items.description: Collingwood franks its strong run of form with an impressive 34-point win over Adelaide, as Crows fans defy pleas from the club and boo Isaac Quaynor.

items.title: Children in state care being lured into 'trap houses'
items.description: The ABC has spoken with experts, advocates and residential care workers as part of a 19-month investigation into the sexual exploitation of children in state care.

items.title: Australia gets first win with Glasgow asleep and the Games yet to open
items.description: Australia's first victory of the Commonwealth Games comes in a surprise extra session as the bowlers start before the opening ceremony.

items.title: Netball agents frustrated as pay talks roll into Glasgow 2026
items.description: Messy and drawn-out pay negotiations are once again overshadowing a major tournament for the Aussie Diamonds.

items.title: Reading has many benefits, here's how to fit it in to a busy life
items.description: More than half of us want to read more. Here's how to find your gateway genre and make that happen.

items.title: Antisemitism 'using Zionism as an excuse', rabbi tells royal commission
items.description: A recent wave of antisemitism has been far-reaching, even targeting Jewish people who are critical of the Israeli government, a royal commission probing the phenomenon has heard.

items.title: Why highly advanced rogue AI has experts scared
items.description: An experimental AI broke out of its containment and hacked a company. Why has this got experts worried?

items.title: Outback hubs prepare for 'amazingly majestic' 2028 solar eclipse
items.description: About 10,000 eclipse chasers are expected to descend on the Northern Territory's Barkly region in two years to stand in the shadow of the moon.

items.title: The intriguing film that casts the 'superior' Jude Law as the insidious Putin
items.description: Cannes darling Oliver Assayas tackles the shadowy forces of our time in his latest film, The Wizard of the Kremlin.

items.title: Nintendo raised prices due to US tariffs. Now, it doesn't want to pass on refunds
items.description: Nintendo has argued it has no duty to pass its refunds onto US consumers. It's the latest in a lengthy tariff fight.

items.title: Judge rejects Woodside's attempt to uncover stink-bomb protest organisers
items.description: Energy giant Woodside fails in its Supreme Court bid to force climate activists to hand over documents about the planning of a stink-bomb protest which prompted the evacuation of its Perth headquarters.

items.title: Taiwanese woman sentenced for attempted murder of Australian exchange student
items.description: Taiwanese media has reported Yang Jinping has been sentenced for the attempted murder of Brisbane exchange student Alex Shorey in 2023.

items.title: Record $60k fine for man behind 'brazen' dump site that will cost $1m to clean
items.description: The owner of one of Victoria's worst illegal dump sites has been handed a record fine of $60,000 and ordered to pay an expected $1 million to clean up the polluted property in Melbourne's outer north-east.

items.title: Insect repellent release leaves 11 staff sick at major SA hospital
items.description: Eleven staff at an Adelaide hospital have become unwell and a dozen emergency beds have been closed, after the accidental release of an "outdoor insect repellent" inside the facility.

items.title: Japanese PM's sleep revelation sparks concern
items.description: It's unlikely Sanae Takaichi intended to start a national conversation when she tweeted about how much rest she gets. A sleep expert says her schedule would be exacting a heavy toll.
